definitions.explanation: A track and field event in which athletes jump over a horizontal bar without any aids.

examples.japanese: {走|はし}り{高跳|たかと}びで{金|きん}メダルを{取|と}った。
examples.english: She won a gold medal in high jump.

examples.japanese: {走|はし}り{高跳|たかと}びの{世界記録|せかいきろく}は2メートル{以上|いじょう}だ。
examples.english: The world record in high jump is over 2 meters.

examples.japanese: {子|こ}どもの{頃|ころ}から{走|はし}り{高跳|たかと}びを{練習|れんしゅう}してきた。
examples.english: I have been practicing high jump since I was a child.

notes:
{走|はし}り{高跳|たかと}び is often shortened to {高跳|たかと}び. Modern high jumpers typically use the "Fosbury Flop" technique, going over the bar backward.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {走|はし}り{高跳|たかと}びの{選手|せんしゅ} (high jumper)
- バーを{越|こ}える (to clear the bar)
- {踏|ふ}み{切|き}る (to take off)

TECHNIQUES:
- {背面跳|はいめんと}び (Fosbury Flop, lit. "back jump")
- {挟|はさ}み{跳|と}び (scissors jump, older technique)
